title: the Fens Rising
premise: True-crime podcaster Oscar Reyes has spent three years in the drowned town of Marrow Fen documenting its coldest case: the disappearance of witness Ada Voss, presumed dead for thirty years. When a faceless client pays him a fortune to prove Ada's murder hasn't happened yet, Oscar realizes the town has been protecting a living secret — and someone intends to finish the job. Following a trail of forged death records and a found family of misfits who raised him, Oscar discovers Ada faked her death to escape the town's founding families, and that his own podcast was bait to flush her out. In the climax at the sinking chapel in the fens, Oscar must choose between exposing the truth that will destroy his found family or burying it forever; he broadcasts everything, saving Ada but losing the only home he ever had.
about_author: I. M. Nakamura is the pen name of a former court stenographer from East Anglia who spent a decade transcribing small-town trials before turning to fiction. Their work is known for marshland atmospherics and mysteries where the archives themselves lie.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of the Dead
chapters.summary: Oscar Reyes, POV. In his cluttered studio above the bait shop, Oscar files episode notes on the thirty-year-old Voss disappearance, establishing his obsessive order and emotional distance. A listener letter hints someone in town knows more. Beat: lonely control masking grief.

chapters.title: Payment in Advance
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. A courier delivers an envelope of cash and a contract: prove Ada Voss's murder hasn't happened — yet. No return address, only a fen reed pressed flat inside. Beat: unease curdling into fascination.

chapters.title: Marrow Fen Rules
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Oscar canvasses the town; old-timers close doors mid-sentence, and his landlady warns him off with tea and threats. Establishes the town's code of silence. Beat: the warmth of community revealed as a wall.

chapters.title: The Found Family Diner
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Oscar and diner cook Marta Ilić, who helped raise him. Marta feeds him free and deflects questions about Ada, but her hands shake. Beat: love complicated by obvious concealment.

chapters.title: Episode Forty-Seven
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. He airs an anniversary episode; downloads spike unnaturally overnight, all traced to one local server. Someone in Marrow Fen is listening closely. Beat: hunter realizing he is prey.

chapters.title: The Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Following the reed clue, Oscar hikes to the half-sunken chapel where Ada was last seen. He finds fresh footprints — impossible after thirty years. Beat: wonder edged with dread.

chapters.title: Records That Lie
chapters.summary: New POV: junior archivist Priya Chandrasekaran. Priya finds Ada's death certificate signed by a doctor who died before the date on it. She emails Oscar anonymously. Beat: quiet courage of a bystander choosing sides.

chapters.title: Tea with the Alderman
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Founding-family patriarch Alderman Crane offers Oscar funding for his podcast — if he drops the case. The threat beneath the courtesy is unmistakable. Beat: temptation as a trap.

chapters.title: What Marta Buried
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. Flashback chapter: young Marta helping a bleeding stranger vanish into the fens decades ago, sworn to silence. Present-day Marta burns a letter. Beat: guilt as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Client Speaks
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. A distorted voice call: the client claims Ada is alive and will be murdered within weeks unless Oscar finds her first. Proof offered: a recent photograph of Ada's eyes. Beat: deadline established, stakes personal.

chapters.title: Priya Comes Forward
chapters.summary: Priya, POV. Priya meets Oscar, reveals the forged records and a pattern: three other 'deaths' in the same decade, all witnesses. Beat: alliance formed over shared fear.

chapters.title: The Bait Shop Basement
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Searching his late foster father's things, Oscar finds a hidden key and a map of the fens marked with a star matching the chapel. His guardian knew. Beat: betrayal of the man he loved most.

chapters.title: Crane's Younger Son
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Oscar confronts Julian Crane, the black-sheep heir who left town, now back and watching Oscar's studio. Julian denies being the client but knows too much. Beat: wary chemistry, possible ally.

chapters.title: Fog Season
chapters.summary: Priya, POV. Priya is followed home; her archive access is revoked. She copies files to a thumb drive anyway. Beat: escalating danger, resolve hardening.

chapters.title: The Star on the Map
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Night expedition to the marked point: a drainage hut stocked with food, blankets, and a woman's worn journal — entries continuing until last month. Beat: hope arriving like a heartbeat.

chapters.title: Ada's Journal, Part One
chapters.summary: Ada Voss, POV (journal excerpts). 1994: Ada witnessed the Cranes' fatal hit-and-run and chose to disappear rather than testify, aided by townsfolk who owed her. Beat: the town's loyalty born of shared sin.

chapters.title: Someone Follows
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Leaving the hut, Oscar is run off the levee road; he survives, but his recorder — with the journal photographed — is stolen. Beat: fear made physical.

chapters.title: The Podcast Goes Quiet
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. With Oscar hospitalized briefly, Marta and the diner regulars quietly guard him, revealing how many townsfolk were part of Ada's escape network. Beat: found family showing its teeth.

chapters.title: Julian's Confession
chapters.summary: Julian, POV. Julian admits his father ordered the original cover-up and that he returned because the family is fracturing — his brother wants the past finished permanently. Beat: reluctant truth-teller.

chapters.title: Ada's Journal, Part Two
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Recent entries: Ada has been dying slowly and wants to come home before the end — which explains the client's 'hasn't happened yet.' Her return would expose everyone. Beat: tragedy reframing the mystery.

chapters.title: Who Pays for Silence
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Oscar traces the payment to a shell company linked not to the Cranes but to the town trust itself — the whole community funded the cover-up. Beat: the villain is everyone and no one.

chapters.title: Marta's Choice
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. Confronted by Oscar, Marta confesses her role and begs him to let Ada die in peace, unexposed. Oscar refuses. Beat: the found family fractures along the fault line of truth.

chapters.title: The Second Contract
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. A second envelope arrives: double the money, new instructions — find Ada and tell no one, or Marta loses the diner. The client isn't protecting Ada; they're managing the timeline. Beat: manipulation unmasked.

chapters.title: Priya Disappears
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Priya misses their meeting; her flat is tossed, thumb drive gone. Guilt drives Oscar from investigator to protector. Beat: cost of the chase made flesh.

chapters.title: Into the Black Fens
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Using his foster father's old paths, Oscar goes off-grid into the deep marsh, following peat-cutters' marks. Weather turns. Beat: descent, both literal and moral.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Hut
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Ada reveals herself to the half-lost Oscar — older, ill, sharp-tongued, alive. She tests him with the question that ruined her: what would he trade for the truth? Beat: meeting the myth.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Ada tells her full story: the crash, the choice, the town that became her accomplice, the loneliness of being dead. Beat: empathy replacing mystery.

chapters.title: The Client Unmasked
chapters.summary: Julian, POV. Julian identifies the voice: not his father but the town solicitor, executor of the trust, who engineered Ada's escape and now controls her ending — and who took Priya. Beat: the puppeteer steps onstage.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. The solicitor offers Oscar everything: Priya safe, Marta's diner secure, Ada's peaceful death — in exchange for the journals and permanent silence. Beat: the devil's bargain, genuinely tempting.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. Marta learns of the deal and, for the first time in thirty years, chooses truth over protection: she gives Oscar the last piece — where Ada hid the original crash evidence. Beat: redemption through betrayal of the lie.

chapters.title: Recovering Priya
chapters.summary: Oscar and Julian, alternating POV. They extract Priya from a locked boathouse; she kept a duplicate drive. The alliance of outsider, heir, and archivist is complete. Beat: found family rebuilt on honesty.

chapters.title: The Evidence in the Peat
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. At the starred site, they recover the tin box: photographs, the driver's confession letter, proof against two generations of Cranes. Beat: the truth made physical, heavy as wet earth.

chapters.title: Alderman's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Alderman Crane, POV. The patriarch, confronted, collapses into confession — he has been waiting thirty years to be caught. Beat: evil revealed as exhausted cowardice.

chapters.title: Deadline Eve
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. The solicitor, exposed, moves to erase Ada tonight. Oscar must choose: broadcast now and doom Ada's anonymity, or stay silent and lose her to murder. Beat: the thematic fulcrum — loyalty versus truth.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. From the chapel ruins with failing signal, Oscar airs Episode Fifty live: Ada's story, the evidence, the names. The town listens in kitchens and cars. Beat: catharsis through exposure.

chapters.title: The Chapel Standoff
chapters.summary: Ada and Oscar, alternating POV. The solicitor comes for Ada; Marta, Julian, and half the town arrive instead, standing between them. The solicitor breaks when the crowd refuses to look away. Beat: collective courage as climax.

chapters.title: After the Water Recedes
chapters.summary: Priya, POV. Arrests, resignations, the trust dissolved. Priya publishes the archive properly. Beat: institutional reckoning, quiet aftermath.

chapters.title: Ada Comes Home
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Legally resurrected, frail Ada walks into the diner on her own feet; Marta serves her the meal she's owed for thirty years. Beat: restoration, earned and unsentimental.

chapters.title: The Last Episode
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Oscar closes the series, admitting his own complicity in consuming other people's tragedies. He keeps the cash — donated to the town archive in Ada's name. Beat: accountability and release.

chapters.title: Rising
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV, epilogue. Spring floods recede; the chapel emerges fully for the first time in decades. Oscar stays in Marrow Fen, no longer invisible, recording nothing — just living. Beat: peace chosen over story.
